headline: Inland Sea Access and Mandatory Bear Safety Registration
reservation: All visitors must register with Parks Canada and receive a safety orientation, specifically regarding polar bears and grizzly bears. There are no facilities; independent travelers must be self-sufficient and confirm all permits with the Naujaat or Rankin Inlet offices prior to departure.

days.title: Reversing Falls and Wager Bay
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from a vessel in Wager Bay

stops.name: Reversing Falls
stops.detail: Witness the powerful tidal phenomenon at the entrance of Wager Bay where water rushes in or out depending on the tide.

stops.name: Douglas Harbour
stops.detail: Navigate the deep fiords that extend from the main bay, framed by high cliffs and potential wildlife sightings.

days.driving: Boat-based travel; allow 4–8 hours depending on tidal currents
days.note: Tidal timing is critical for safely navigating the Reversing Falls.

days.title: Cultural History and Tundra
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Wager Bay shoreline

stops.name: Hudson's Bay Company Post ruins
stops.detail: Explore the remains of the 1920s-era trading post at Ford Lake, a testament to the region's fur trade history.

stops.name: Sila River
stops.detail: Hike the river banks to see unique geological formations and arctic wildflowers.

days.driving: Hiking; allow 4–6 hours for exploring the ruins and river
days.note: Ancient Inuit tent rings are scattered throughout; do not disturb archaeological sites.

days.title: Wildlife Monitoring and Coastal Bluffs
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from the southern shore

stops.name: Cape Fullerton
stops.detail: While just outside the park, this area is a critical historical and wildlife gateway often visited in conjunction with the park.

stops.name: Pikwitonei Inlet
stops.detail: Search the shoreline for marine mammals such as seals and the occasional polar bear.

days.driving: Boat travel; conditions vary by wind and ice
days.note: High concentrations of bears occur in late summer; constant vigilance is required.

intel.title: Gateway Storage
intel.text: No road access exists to Ukkusiksalik. Vehicles are left in Naujaat (Repulse Bay) or Rankin Inlet; check with local municipalities for designated long-term areas.

intel.title: Communication Gap
intel.text: There is no cellular coverage. Reliable communication requires a satellite phone; ensure you have the contact numbers for the Parks Canada duty office and local search and rescue.

intel.title: Community Staging
intel.text: Buy all stove fuel and supplies in Naujaat or Coral Harbour. There are absolutely no services, buildings, or supply points within the park boundaries.

intel.title: Tidal Windows
intel.text: The Reversing Falls are only navigable at specific slack tide windows. Consult local Inuk guides who have intimate knowledge of these dangerous waters.

intel.title: Marine Logistics
intel.text: Access is mostly by boat from Naujaat during the ice-free weeks of August. Winter access via snowmobile is possible but requires specialized extreme-cold equipment.

plan.arrival: Fly into Naujaat and meet your licensed Inuit outfitter for a gear check and boat loading; finalize your bear safety plan.
plan.vehicle: Strictly boat or snowmobile; no passenger cars or RVs are used in this region. Confirm vessel seaworthiness for Arctic waters.
plan.goldenHour: The Ford Lake ruins offer a hauntingly beautiful silhouette against the low Arctic sun in late August.
